html:
SMTO-LLM-0050 — The AI model asked for too many actions at once

GUID: 5bae26bd-931b-4054-a5a7-e0d9f79d96f6
Slug: model-call-limit-exceeded
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: llm

What happened

  • In a single reply, the model asked for more actions than one step allows, or for none when one was required. SMTO ran none of them.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the steps already shown for this task in the conversation and note which ones finished before the error. Work finished before this reply still stands, so you only need SMTO to continue, not redo it.
  2. Split a large request into smaller parts and send them one after another, for example one folder or one file at a time. A narrower request leads the model to plan fewer actions in a single reply.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and pick a different model for Main (and Helper, if one is set), then save. Some models try to do everything in one reply; another model may pace its actions better.
  4. Send a new message asking SMTO to continue from where it stopped, without repeating the steps that already finished. SMTO can then pick up the remaining work without redoing what's already done.

What success looks like

  • SMTO carries out the next actions one reply at a time and the task keeps moving.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or your AI model server. You don't need to shorten or clear the conversation; this problem isn't caused by its length.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The number of tool calls in the response is outside the allowed range for this decision (more than 64 for an Agent decision, not exactly one for a named internal step, or none despite a tool_calls finish), so the whole batch was rejected before dispatch.

What this means

  • The number of tool calls exceeds the allowed bound for this decision; protocol normalization and the caller's stricter limit are separate checks. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • The number of tool calls exceeds the allowed bound for this decision; protocol normalization and the caller's stricter limit are separate checks.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the number of calls with the current decision's advertised bound; a normal single-call decision differs from a bounded batch.

How to fix it

  • Compare the tool_calls count in Technical details with the limit in the message (max_calls: 64 for Agent decisions, 1 for named internal turns). Narrow the request so the model plans fewer calls per turn, or route to a model that follows the advertised call limits; keep the limits in place.
  • Use the advertised bounded sequence/parallel interfaces and reduce calls per model decision. Keep admission limits in place.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The complete response stays within the applicable call bound and every call validates.

What not to do

  • Do not replay prior successful operations to repair a later model response.
  • Do not disable protocol validation or treat this representation failure as input-context overflow.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
